description: A wav sample player and recorder with a cyclic time-stretch, cue and loop cursors, a four-stage envelope and polyphonic pitch tracking

params.text: Sets the output volume, 0 to 100%
Sets where playback begins and the attack starts, as a percentage of the sample
Sets where playback ends and the release starts, as a percentage of the sample
Sets where a loop begins, as a percentage of the sample
Sets where a loop ends, as a percentage of the sample
Sets the crossfade at a loop join, the fade before the end of the sample, and the fade in and out of a recording, 1ms to 10 seconds
Sets how long the envelope takes to rise, 1ms to 10 seconds
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall to the sustain level, 1ms to 10 seconds
Sets the level the envelope holds at, 0% to 100%
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall to silence, 1ms to 10 seconds
Chooses whether playback is started by a trigger or held open by a gate
Chooses what a trigger does in trigger mode: Start/Stop alternates, Restart plays from the cue start every time
Plays between the loop cursors over and over instead of stopping at the cue end
Plays the sample backwards, from the cue end towards the cue start
Reverses the playback direction at the cursors instead of jumping back, so the sample runs forwards and backwards in turn
Starts recording at once; it is available only while no sample is loaded or recorded, so the sample has to be cleared first
Sets the level of the recording inputs, 0 to 200%
Passes the recording inputs through to the outputs
Loads the previous file in the same folder
Loads the next file in the same folder
Starts playback by hand, working as the PLAY jack does
Moves the cue and loop cursors to the nearest zero crossings, which stops loop clicks; it should be off for one-cycle waveforms
Lengthens or shortens the sample without changing its pitch, 1% to 999%, with 100% leaving it alone
Sets the length of the repeated cycle the time-stretch is built from, 1ms to 99ms

inputs.text: Starts playback: a trigger in trigger mode, or held high in gate mode
Shifts the output volume, added to the VOL knob
Raises the playback pitch one octave per volt; a polyphonic cable here plays one voice per channel
The left channel to be recorded; recording is only possible with a cable in here
The right channel to be recorded, which makes the recording stereo

outputs.text: The left channel of the sample, or the whole of a mono file duplicated
The right channel of the sample, or the whole of a mono file duplicated
A 1ms pulse at whichever points are ticked under 'EOC pulse from'
A 1ms pulse when the release stage ends

notes: nothing plays until a sample is loaded or recorded: right-click the panel and use Load Sample, or right-click the waveform display.
the REC button is only active while the sample slot is empty, so a loaded or recorded sample has to be cleared before recording again.
there is no STOP button or jack; in trigger mode with Start/Stop a second trigger stops playback, and in Restart mode playback is stopped by moving the MODE switch to Gate.
stretching a sample gives the characteristic metallic sound of cyclic time-stretching, most audible when slowing down; the XFD and SIZ knobs trade one artefact against another.
menu: Load Sample — opens a file chooser for the sample this module plays
Save FULL Sample — writes the whole sample to a wav file
Save CUE Region — writes the part between the cue cursors to a wav file
Save LOOP Region — writes the part between the loop cursors to a wav file
Trim Sample after Save — keeps only the saved part in memory afterwards, instead of keeping the whole sample
Save Oversampled — writes the file at the module's internal rate, twice Rack's, for editing elsewhere
Select Samples Root — picks a folder, after which a Samples Browser submenu appears for loading
Anti-aliasing filter — adds two-times oversampling and a 20kHz lowpass before the outputs
Polyphonic OUTs — carries the V/Oct polyphony through to the outputs; with it off every voice is summed into single-channel outputs
Polyphonic Master IN — lets the VOL CV jack take a polyphonic cable matching the V/Oct channels, for per-voice velocity
Auto Monitor Off — turns monitoring off by itself once a recording stops
EOC pulse from — a submenu of seven points, each ticked or not, at which the EOC output sends a pulse: TRG/GATE (stop), CUE END, CUE START, LOOP END, LOOP START, PING and PONG
Disable NAV Buttons — stops the panel navigation buttons from loading anything, so they cannot be pressed by accident
Reset Cursors — puts the cue and loop cursors back to 0% and 100%
